text:
akash: FYI — customer 'acme-pay' reporting intermittent 401s on GitHub Actions deploys. Only happens when job matrix has parallelism >1. Single job runs succeed. Repro steps below.

katie: ack. Any error payloads from the runner or deploy bot?

akash: paste from runner logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-15T14:02:12Z runner-2 INFO request to /v1/deploy -> 401
{"error":"invalid_token","message":"service account credential expired"}
2026-02-15T14:02:12Z runner-2 DEBUG token_expiry: 2026-02-15T15:02:12Z (3600s)
2026-02-15T14:02:12Z runner-1 INFO request to /v1/deploy -> 200
```
Note: runner-1 and runner-2 are concurrent matrix jobs on the same host.

rob: interesting — same host, different processes. Could be token cache per-process vs per-host race. Do we use ephemeral impersonated tokens from our token proxy?

akash: yes, GHA runners call our internal token proxy at `/internal/iam/impersonate` which issues ephemeral SA tokens (TTL configured at 3600s). I repro'd locally by launching 4 parallel jobs via `act` and saw ~25% of runs 401.

samir: any clock-skew in the host? If one process sees expiry earlier it might try to refresh but race conditions could return slightly different expiry claims.

akash: checked NTP — hosts are within 2s. But digging into token proxy responses I found small TTL jitter: sometimes `expires_in` returned 3592 or 3607. That plus rounding + our 5s refresh threshold causes a few tokens to be considered expired prematurely in some processes.

katie: can you include the exact HTTP flow you used to repro?

akash: repro steps:
1) Checkout repo with matrix strategy (4 parallel jobs).
2) In each job run `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $(curl -s http://token-proxy.local/impersonate?sa=ci-deployer)" https://deploy.internal/api/v1/trigger`
3) Observe 401 in subset of runs.

Example token-proxy reply (sanitized headers):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{"access_token":"ya29....","expires_in":3592}
```
Then another parallel call returns `expires_in`:3607.

rob: ok that matches. With per-process caching we store token and expiry timestamp locally; if one process stores expires_in=3592 and another 3607, the one with 3592 may hit the refresh flow earlier and race. If refresh is slow or fails we get 401.

samir: mitigation options: (A) adjust token-proxy to include a grace window (i.e., return `expires_in` slightly higher / or our client should add grace), (B) make runner use host-level token cache keyed by SA so matrix jobs reuse same token when on same host, (C) add automatic 401->retry-with-new-token with jittered backoff.

akash: I prototyped C locally — on 401 we force a token refresh and retry once; reduces failures to near 0 but it's a bandaid.

katie: what's the least-privilege impact? Are tokens scoped overly broad? Could shorter TTLs cause more renewals and worsen race?

rob: current TTL is 3600s for convenience. Shorter TTL raises frequency of renews and increases chance of collision. For least privilege, the SA `ci-deployer` has only `cloudkms.encrypt, storage.objects.get, redwood.deploy` — looks fine. Not an issue here.

akash: I also noticed our token-proxy sometimes rounds `expires_in` from server returned `exp` claim which is in seconds; there's a floor/ceil bug where sub-second differences produce +/-15s in `expires_in`. That seems like the root cause.

samir: proposal: 1) fix token-proxy rounding bug (patch queued), 2) add 30s safety margin in runner token check (client-side), 3) implement host-level cache for tokens keyed by SA+audience if runner host has multiple matrix workers.

katie: agree. Can we triage severity? Customer impact: deploys fail ~1 in 4 on large parallel runs — they're blocking CI gating production deploys. Mark P1 for support escalation.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-3421 — Escalate: acme-pay intermittent 401s on parallel GHA matrix runs. Assigned to eng-infra.

rob: I'll own the host-cache change (small change to runner daemon, estimate 2d). akash can verify the proxy fix once merged. samir take the proxy rounding fix. katie can keep customer notified, include temporary workaround: set matrix concurrency to 1 or add retry logic in workflow (retry on 401 once with 5s backoff).

akash: I pushed a small workflow snippet for retry workaround:
```
- name: Trigger deploy
  run: |
    token=$(curl -s http://token-proxy.local/impersonate?sa=ci-deployer)
    for i in 1 2; do
      if curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -f https://deploy.internal/api/v1/trigger; then break; fi
      sleep 5
      token=$(curl -s http://token-proxy.local/impersonate?sa=ci-deployer)
    done
```
This is messy, but reduced failures in repro.

katie: created a short customer note with workaround and ETA for fixes. Will share once rob/samir confirm timelines.

samir: patch PR #2896 opened for token-proxy rounding — includes unit test for fractional `exp` handling.

rob: PR for runner host-cache coming in by EOD tomorrow. I'll add metrics: token-refresh-rate and 401-retry-count.

akash: I'll monitor acme-pay runs and attach logs to SUP-3421. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
